phone.help: The server cannot tell whether a phone reaches it: only a phone can. Scan the code of an address with a phone — on the guests' Wi-Fi or on mobile data, as a participant would be. A tested address is offered first.
phone.scan: Scan with a phone: the page tells this one it got through.

why.title: Not reached? The usual causes
why.network: Not the same network: a local address (192.168…, 10…) only answers phones on that network — the guests' Wi-Fi is often another one; on mobile data it never answers.
why.isolation: Isolated guests: many guest or public Wi-Fi networks keep devices from seeing each other. Use the public address, or a network without it.
why.firewall: A firewall: the machine may refuse incoming connections on the application's port.
why.public: A public address needs a name pointing to the machine and its port open from the internet (or a reverse proxy) — and https for phones to install the app.
why.docker: Docker Desktop, a bridge network: the container cannot see the machine's own addresses — set them in HOST_LAN_IPS.

access.firstAdmin: Local mode: the name that will administer the instance (they sign in with it). Changes from the web also need ADMIN_TOKEN.
access.oidcAdmin: With an identity provider, the administrator role comes from it (or from `qd user:set-role`).
